title: The top nonzero cohomology of a pseudo-coherent complex is finitely presented
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] be pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], and let $n\in\mathbf Z$. If $H^i(K)=0$ for every $i>n$, then the cohomology sheaf $H^n(K)$ is a finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. No coherence or Noetherian assumption is made on $X$.

source.place: Tag 08DN, lemma-finite-cohomology, part (2), with m=n-1; pseudo-coherent implies m-pseudo-coherent for every integer m.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$. By [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], choose a neighbourhood $U$ and a bounded-above finite free complex $P^\bullet$ representing $K|_U$, with $P^i=0$ for $i>N$. Exact open restriction [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact] preserves kernels, images and cokernels, hence $H^i(P^\bullet)=H^i(K)|_U=0$ for $i>n$. Its terms are finite locally free by [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf]. Increase the bound to $r=\max(N,n)$.

source.place: Tag 08DN, lemma-finite-cohomology, proof of (2), with the top-degree cancellation of (1); use the scheme-local bounded-above finite-free characterization of pseudo-coherence.

proof.text: Induct on the nonnegative integer $r-n$ to obtain, after shrinking around $x$, a finite locally free complex representing $K$ and zero above $n$. For $r=n$ use the supplied complex. If $r>n$, its $r$th cohomology is zero by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-top-cancellation] on the current open scheme at $x$: this replaces the complex by a quasi-isomorphic finite locally free complex zero above $r-1$. Exact restriction preserves the vanishing above $n$; the quasi-isomorphism preserves all cohomology, so the induction hypothesis applies with $(r-1)-n=(r-n)-1$. Only finitely many shrinkings are required.

source.place: Tag 08DN, lemma-finite-cohomology, proof of (2), with the top-degree cancellation of (1); use the scheme-local bounded-above finite-free characterization of pseudo-coherence.

proof.text: Call the final complex $Q^\bullet$ on $V$. Shrink $V$ around $x$ to trivialize just $Q^{n-1}$ and $Q^n$, using [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], of ranks $a,b\geq0$. As $Q^{n+1}=0$, the definition of cohomology gives $H^n(K)|_V\cong H^n(Q^\bullet)=\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal O_V^{\oplus a}\xrightarrow{d^{n-1}}\mathcal O_V^{\oplus b})$. Exact restriction justifies the first identification after this final shrinking. This is a finite presentation at $x$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Since $x$ was arbitrary, it proves the claim; the empty scheme is vacuous.
